name: Akuku
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog refs are only 1914 specimens, sociolinguistic survey (Decker et al. 2024) and classification papers; no phonology

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, John Muniru, David Onoja, Lewinan Andrew & Samuel Eju. 2024. A Sociolinguistic Profile of Five Southern Northwestern Edoid Languages in Southern Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2024-012. Dallas: SIL International. 72 pp. (Glottolog ref 700271; Glottolog MED for akuk1235)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 8.3 'Phonetic inventories' (pp.27-30) gives pooled consonant/vowel charts and labialization/palatalization notes for Okpe, Orake, Akhukhu, Okpamheri; Appendix F p.49: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no analysis of tones and no in-depth analysis of other phonological or phonetic features.' The 222-item Akhukhu wordlist (Akuku town, 22 Sept 2021) is mostly untoned. Sec. 4 p.6: prior information on Akhukhu limited to Thomas 1914:137-139, Jungraithmayr & Ganslmayr 1986:39, Lewis 2015.

sources.citation: Lewis, Demola. 2015. Deciphering Aborigines and Migrants from Cognation and Topography in North-Western Edo. Lengua y Migracion 7(1): 29-51.
sources.note: Nothing; lexicostatistics and settlement history only ('The Akuku speak an independent language which has blended much with its contact speech forms'; Akuku-Somorika 71%, Akuku-Enwa 60%).

sources.citation: Egbokhare, Francis O. 2011. The Sound of Meaning. Inaugural lecture, University of Ibadan.
sources.note: Nothing on Akuku; mentions Akuku only as a one-village Akoko-Edo community whose speech others find 'distant and difficult' and as a village where Edo-North documentation tapes were recorded.

sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben Ohi. 1989. Edoid. In J. Bendor-Samuel (ed.), The Niger-Congo Languages, 291-304. Lanham: UPA.
sources.note: 'Okpe-Akuku-Idesa' appears in the classification list only; no Akuku data.

sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben Ohiomamhe. 1989. Comparative Edoid: Phonology and Lexicon (Delta Series 6). Port Harcourt: University of Port Harcourt Press.
sources.note: No Akuku data: Akuku appears only in the classification (sec. 1.3.4 'Okpe-Akuku-Idesa', Southern NWE) and as 'a NWE village' (p.11); ch. 4 sketches cover Oloma, Emhalhe, Ibilo, Uhami, Ehueun, Ukue but not Okpe-Akuku-Idesa. Sec. 3.5 'Tone' (pp.47-48) is a family-level statement that Edoid languages have tone systems (three levels, or two levels with/without downstep); the word 'stress' does not occur.

sources.citation: Egbokhare, Francis O. 2022. Unification and harmonization of Afenmai languages: Issues and challenges. In M. E. Ekpenyong & I. I. Udoh (eds.), Current Issues in Descriptive Linguistics and Digital Humanities (Festschrift Urua), 333-342. Singapore: Springer.
